PURPOSE: Think like a 14th-15th century pharmacist. Text is 95% abbreviations. Validate character mappings by whether they produce coherent pharmaceutical abbreviation sequences.
CORE_PRINCIPLE: The text is NOT random gibberish. It is ABBREVIATION SEQUENCES. Each character mapping must be tested by: can the decrypted words be parsed into real pharmaceutical abbreviations that follow recipe logic?

EXAMPLE_RECIPES.validity: REAL - oil-based salt remedy for pain

VALIDATION_RULES.RULE_1: Each abbreviation in a sequence must have MEANING - no unknown abbreviations allowed
VALIDATION_RULES.RULE_2: Abbreviations must follow PHARMACEUTICAL GRAMMAR - what can follow what matters
VALIDATION_RULES.RULE_3: Recipes must follow recognizable STRUCTURE - ingredient → preparation → action → indication
VALIDATION_RULES.RULE_4: Medical conditions (dol, febr, etc.) require ACTION before them or PREPOSITION
VALIDATION_RULES.RULE_5: Actions (dar, da, fac) require either INGREDIENT or TARGET to make sense
VALIDATION_RULES.RULE_6: Prepositions (ad, per, in) must connect ACTIONS to TARGETS or ACTIONS to INGREDIENTS
VALIDATION_RULES.RULE_7: A sequence is PHARMACEUTICAL if it parses 100% and follows recipe structure

CHARACTER_MAPPING_TESTING_PROCESS.STEP_1: Start with locked characters (s, a, l, d, o, r) - these are PROVEN to work
CHARACTER_MAPPING_TESTING_PROCESS.STEP_2: For each unknown EVA character, test mapping to different Latin letters
CHARACTER_MAPPING_TESTING_PROCESS.STEP_3: For each test mapping, decrypt ALL words containing that character
CHARACTER_MAPPING_TESTING_PROCESS.STEP_4: Parse each decrypted word into abbreviation sequences using the grammar model above
CHARACTER_MAPPING_TESTING_PROCESS.STEP_5: Count: how many words parse into 100% valid pharmaceutical abbreviations?
CHARACTER_MAPPING_TESTING_PROCESS.STEP_6: Accept mapping ONLY IF 60%+ of words parse into valid pharmaceutical sequences
CHARACTER_MAPPING_TESTING_PROCESS.STEP_7: Lock that mapping and move to next character (prevents collisions)
CHARACTER_MAPPING_TESTING_PROCESS.STEP_8: Build incremental mapping: locked + validated character by character

WHAT_MAKES_A_CHARACTER_MAPPING_VALID.MUST_HAVE: 60%+ of words containing the character decrypt to 100% valid pharmaceutical abbreviation sequences
WHAT_MAKES_A_CHARACTER_MAPPING_VALID.MUST_NOT_HAVE: Gibberish mixed with abbreviations is INVALID - all parts must be recognizable abbreviations
WHAT_MAKES_A_CHARACTER_MAPPING_VALID.MUST_SHOW: Pattern of coherent pharmaceutical recipes, not random pharmaceutical words scattered in noise
WHAT_MAKES_A_CHARACTER_MAPPING_VALID.MUST_AVOID: Collisions - each EVA character maps to ONE unique Latin letter

KEY_INSIGHT: A medieval pharmacist reading abbreviated recipes would recognize EVERY abbreviation. If 60%+ of decrypted words parse into recognizable pharmaceutical sequences, the mapping is CORRECT. If decrypted words contain unrecognizable letter combinations mixed with abbreviations, the mapping is WRONG.
